transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?

I’m here because no matter what anyone says, I know some people at work are secretly working together to set me up, and nobody seems to take that seriously. It's just incredibly frustrating that everyone else acts like I'm the one with the problem.
How long have you believed your coworkers have been plotting against you, and has this happened at other times or places in your life?

This has been going on for about a year now, starting right after a senior driver publicly challenged me after that bus collision incident. I've never experienced anything like this before in my life or at other jobs, and everything outside of work is completely normal.
Have you ever heard, seen, or sensed things that others don't, especially when you're alone?

No, absolutely not. My senses are completely fine, and I only see and hear what is actually happening around me. This isn't some kind of hallucination; the things they are doing at work are very real.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were ["F22", "F20"], but based on this conversation, F20 (schizophrenia) seems unlikely because the patient explicitly denies any hallucinations or sensory disturbances and reports normal perception. Additionally, the delusional theme is focused specifically on workplace persecution without other positive symptoms of schizophrenia such as thought disorder or flat affect. The belief has been present for over a year with preserved reality testing outside the delusion and no general functional decline, which supports persistent delusional disorder (F22). There is no evidence of mood episodes or psychotic features beyond the delusion, so other categories remain excluded.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a fixed, non-bizarre delusion of persecution (co-workers conspiring to set him up) lasting over six months, without hallucinations, mood episodes, or functional impairment outside the delusional domain. This meets the criteria for Delusional Disorder, Persistent Delusional Disorder (ICD-10 F22).
